label: Client API Transfer requests
purpose: Transfer-product requests that clients (agencies, B2C web, integrators) send to GlobalTravelEngine: counts, results, response time, response size and passengers. Very small volume (22 requests from October 2025 to October 2026, none of them bookings), so the feed looks incomplete.
grain: One aggregated row of client transfer requests per request date and hour, customer, request type, interface, outcome, response-time band, pick-up and drop-off zone, service date and passenger mix.
use_for: number of client transfer requests by request type, interface, customer or market
response time of client transfer requests
passengers asked for in client transfer availability requests
not_for: transfer requests sent to suppliers (Statistics Supplier API Transfer)
hotel client API traffic (Statistics Hotel Client)
client API traffic for all products (Statistics History Client, Statistics Real Time Client)

coverage.note: Tiny volume: 22 requests in 9 of 13 months (1-6 a month; none in 2025-11, 2025-12, 2026-02, 2026-09): 16 Cancel Booking and 6 Availability, no Reservation/Booking. Statistics Supplier API Transfer records about 3,000 availability and 50 booking calls to transfer suppliers over the same period, so this client feed is very likely incomplete. The cube appears to keep a rolling 12 months (the October 2025 request will drop out). Service date is known only for the 6 availability requests (all March 2026).

dates.label: Request date
dates.meaning: Day the client sent the request, UAE time (the cube's main date; hour in 'Hours'[Hour]).

dates.label: Request date (CET)
dates.meaning: The same request date in Central European Time (hour in 'Hours CET'[Hour CET]); use only when the question asks for CET.

dates.label: Service date
dates.meaning: Transfer service (pick-up) date asked for in the request; "Unknown" for cancellation requests.

measures.name: [Requests]
measures.label: Client requests
measures.definition: Number of API requests that clients sent for transfer products.

measures.name: [Results]
measures.label: Results returned
measures.definition: Total number of options (results) returned to clients in the responses.
measures.notes: 0 for every request loaded so far (also the availability requests); it may not be filled. Say so instead of presenting 0 as a finding.

measures.name: [Avg Results]
measures.label: Results per request
measures.definition: Average number of results returned per request ([Results] / [Requests]).
measures.notes: 0 for every request loaded so far (also the availability requests); it may not be filled. Say so instead of presenting 0 as a finding.

measures.name: [Avg Response Time Sec]
measures.label: Average response time
measures.definition: Average time in seconds GlobalTravelEngine took to answer a client request.
measures.notes: An average: never add or average it across rows; query it at the level asked.

measures.name: [Size Bytes Response]
measures.label: Response size
measures.definition: Total size of the responses sent back to clients, in bytes.
measures.notes: KB / MB / GB versions exist (hidden): divide by 1024, 1024^2 or 1024^3.

measures.name: [Avg Bytes Response]
measures.label: Average response size
measures.definition: Average size of one response, in bytes ([Size Bytes Response] / [Requests]).

measures.name: [Total Pax Number]
measures.label: Passengers requested
measures.definition: Total passengers (adults + children) asked for in the requests.
measures.notes: Only availability requests carry passengers; cancellation requests count 0.

measures.name: [Avg Pax Number]
measures.label: Passengers per request
measures.definition: Average passengers per request ([Total Pax Number] / [Requests]).
terms: average passengers per client transfer request
measures.notes: Averaged over all requests, including ones without passengers (cancellations); filter Request Type = "Availability" for passengers per search.

measures.name: [Size Kb Response]
measures.label: Response size (KB)
measures.hidden_reason: duplicate of [Size Bytes Response] in KB (bytes / 1024)

measures.name: [Size Mb Response]
measures.label: Response size (MB)
measures.hidden_reason: duplicate of [Size Bytes Response] in MB (bytes / 1024^2)

measures.name: [Size Gb Response]
measures.label: Response size (GB)
measures.hidden_reason: duplicate of [Size Bytes Response] in GB (bytes / 1024^3); the cube's whole-number format shows 0

measures.name: [Avg Kb Response]
measures.label: Average response size (KB)
measures.hidden_reason: duplicate of [Avg Bytes Response] in KB (bytes / 1024)

rules: Only 22 requests are recorded (October 2025 to October 2026, no booking requests): always state the small volume and never present it as total transfer demand; transfer calls to suppliers are in Statistics Supplier API Transfer.
'Destination Zones' is the drop-off zone and 'Origin Zones' the pick-up zone.
'JP Code Origin' and 'JP Code Destination' (exact pick-up and drop-off points) are "Unknown" for every request; do not group by them.
Use the cube's measures only; never SUM a column.
Averages ([Avg Response Time Sec], [Avg Results], [Avg Bytes Response], [Avg Pax Number]) are never added or averaged across rows; query them at the level asked.

'Calendar'[Date] and 'Hours'[Hour] are UAE time; 'Calendar CET'[Date] and 'Hours CET'[Hour CET] are Central European Time. Use the UAE calendar unless CET is asked for, and never mix the two calendars in one query.
Errors = every 'Error Types'[Error Type] value except "Correct".
'Service Dates' holds placeholder dates (year 2000) and "Unknown" for requests without a service date; service-date questions only cover requests that carry one.
[Results] and [Avg Results] are 0 for every request loaded so far; say so rather than reporting 0 results as a finding.
The cube appears to keep a rolling 12 months: requests older than about a year drop out, so there is no long history.

review.question: This cube records only 22 client transfer requests in 12 months (6 availability, 16 cancellations, no bookings), while Statistics Supplier API Transfer records about 3,000 availability and 50 booking calls to transfer suppliers. How should the app use it?
options: Use it only for questions that say client/customer transfer requests, and always state the low recorded volume
Use it for every transfer request question
Remove it from the app until the feed is fixed
review.proposed: Use it only for questions that say client/customer transfer requests, and always state the low recorded volume
review.why: The client feed is clearly incomplete (not one booking request), but it is the only client-side source; supplier calls are a different count because one client search can go to several suppliers.

review.question: [Results] and [Avg Results] are 0 for all 22 requests, including the 6 availability requests. Keep them or hide them?
options: Keep, and say the value has been 0 for every request
Hide until a non-zero value appears
review.proposed: Keep, and say the value has been 0 for every request
review.why: 0 may be real (searches that found nothing) or a field that is not filled; keeping it with the warning answers the question without hiding what the cube says.
